name: Taste Bridge
benefit: Turn different interests into a shared starting point. Two to five people can contribute named artists, films, books, or other supported interests without needing the same taste.
try: Add Nina Simone / Music and Spirited Away / Film for two people. Choose Find our bridge. Inspect Shared Ground, The Bridge, and The Wild Card, then save a discovery or explore it further.
lookFor: Participant attribution connects the submitted interests to their resolved Qloo entities. The three result roles offer different ways into the returned discoveries; a role can be absent if the evidence does not support it.
technical: Qloo Search resolves the named interests and Insights retrieves using their combined anchors. This is group-conditioned retrieval—not proof that each participant likes every result. Names stay in browser-session memory.

name: What If? Explorer
benefit: Try a different version of your day without losing the original. Start from a current journey, a saved door, or new named interests, and compare alternatives beside an unchanged starting snapshot.
try: Choose Use this starting point. Enter “I only have two hours. I want something completely different.” Review and apply recognized changes, edit the controls if needed, then choose Explore this what-if.
lookFor: The result explains what actually changed. Compare original and alternative discoveries; change the scenario again, save a result, or restore the original scenario. An unchanged result is shown honestly rather than called a new match.
technical: Supported phrases map to editable controls through disclosed rules. Cultural routing changes trigger Qloo retrieval; time, budget, and movement are local planning context, not verified availability, price, health, or accessibility filters.

name: Discovery Debate
benefit: Question a recommendation instead of accepting a black-box answer. Ask for its evidence, disagree with the direction, or request a more unexpected alternative, then continue the conversation about a returned discovery.
try: Select a current or saved recommendation, or generate one. Ask what evidence supports it and send the challenge. Next choose Retrieve something more unexpected and send it. Select a returned candidate to debate, save, or explore.
lookFor: The interpretation preview explains the action before submission. Transcript turns identify the recommendation being discussed. Evidence-only replies and new retrievals are visibly different, so judges can follow what actually happened.
technical: Evidence replies read recorded result metadata locally. Alternative requests use Qloo with the selected entity, supported feedback, and seen-entity exclusions. Unsupported wording asks for an explicit action; this is a rule-based evidence conversation, not unrestricted AI chat.

name: Discovery Lab
benefit: Explore different directions without losing the path you started on. Checkpoints preserve a starting moment, independent branches let you try different approaches, and side-by-side comparison helps you choose which discovery to continue.
try: Choose Explore in Discovery Lab from a journey, or start in the Lab with named interests and your selected Qloo connection. Open Follow the Thread to create the starting checkpoint, open a door, and mark a result Keep. Restore that checkpoint and try Take the Wild Door. Under Compare branches, select the shared checkpoint and both sibling branches.
lookFor: Compare each branch’s discoveries, explanations, source information, conditions, and feedback from the same starting point. Favorite and resume the path you prefer. Restore a checkpoint without erasing the sibling branch; reload to see completed exploration restored.
technical: Live branches use the selected shared Demo or personal Qloo connection through the shared discovery provider. Branch strategies influence retrieval direction, not a measured novelty score or guaranteed different results. Lab histories and checkpoints remain browser-local, including for signed-in users. Restored results are saved history, not new requests; prepared examples are a separate authored mode.
